entries.meaning_intent: To carelessly expose yourself to theft, harm, or ridicule through your own negligence — the phrase implies the victim shares the blame for having invited the opportunity.
entries.english_equivalent: To ask for trouble / to be an easy target
entries.example_es: Dejó el celular sobre la mesa y se fue a bailar — ¡eso es dar papaya!
entries.example_en: He left his phone on the table and went off to dance — he was practically asking for it!

entries.meaning_intent: To seize on an opportunity someone else carelessly created — the mirror image of 'dar papaya'; describes the opportunist, not the victim.
entries.english_equivalent: To take the bait / to pounce on an easy opening
entries.example_es: Como dejó la puerta abierta, el ladrón cogió papaya y entró.
entries.example_en: Since he left the door open, the thief took the bait and walked right in.

entries.meaning_intent: To be going through a stretch of bad luck, as if cursed or jinxed — used for both people and situations.
entries.english_equivalent: To be jinxed / on a losing streak
entries.example_es: Se me dañó el carro otra vez, estoy salado esta semana.
entries.example_en: My car broke down again — I'm jinxed this week.

entries.idiom: Meterse en camisa de once varas
entries.literal_translation: To put on a shirt made of eleven yards of cloth
entries.meaning_intent: To take on a problem far more complicated than necessary, often one that isn't even yours to solve.
entries.english_equivalent: To bite off more than you can chew / to get in over your head
entries.example_es: No te metás en camisa de once varas resolviendo el problema de esos dos.
entries.example_en: Don't bite off more than you can chew trying to fix those two people's problem.

entries.literal_translation: For the hand to slip away from someone
entries.meaning_intent: To overdo something — go further than intended, whether in punishment, a joke, spending, or a recipe.
entries.english_equivalent: To overdo it / to take it too far
entries.example_es: Se le fue la mano con el picante, esto casi no se puede comer.
entries.example_en: He overdid it with the chili — this is almost inedible.

entries.literal_translation: To walk around stepping on eggs
entries.meaning_intent: To move through a delicate or risky situation with extreme, deliberate caution.
entries.english_equivalent: To walk on eggshells / to tread carefully
entries.example_es: Desde la pelea, ando pisando huevos con mi jefe.
entries.example_en: Since the argument, I've been walking on eggshells around my boss.

entries.literal_translation: To catch someone on the way down
entries.meaning_intent: To repeatedly take advantage of someone once you've identified them as an easy, passive target.
entries.english_equivalent: To walk all over someone / to use someone as a pushover
entries.example_es: Deja de dejarte coger de bajada, pon límites en esa amistad.
entries.example_en: Stop letting them walk all over you — set some limits in that friendship.

entries.meaning_intent: To take precautions and avoid creating opportunities for others to take advantage of or harm you — the advice form of 'dar papaya'.
entries.english_equivalent: Don't make yourself an easy target / don't ask for it
entries.example_es: En esa zona hay que ser vivo y no dar papaya con el celular.
entries.example_en: In that area you have to be smart and not flash your phone around.

entries.meaning_intent: To snap out of complacency, focus, and start putting in real effort — a call to urgency or discipline.
entries.english_equivalent: To get your act together / to step it up
entries.example_es: Si querés pasar el examen, ponete las pilas desde ya.
entries.example_en: If you want to pass the exam, you'd better get your act together starting now.

entries.meaning_intent: To work, especially hard or grinding work; derived from 'camello' as slang for a job or tough task.
entries.english_equivalent: To grind / to work hard
entries.example_es: Toca camellar duro este mes para pagar el arriendo.
entries.example_en: We've got to grind hard this month to make rent.

entries.meaning_intent: A job, or more specifically a difficult, tiring task or workload.
entries.english_equivalent: A grind / a slog
entries.example_es: Ese proyecto fue un camello, no dormí en toda la semana.
entries.example_en: That project was a real grind — I didn't sleep all week.

entries.meaning_intent: To pool money among a group of people for a shared purchase or gift.
entries.english_equivalent: To chip in / to split the cost as a group
entries.example_es: Hagamos una vaca para el regalo de cumpleaños de David.
entries.example_en: Let's all chip in for David's birthday present.

entries.meaning_intent: To be in serious financial or personal trouble, at rock bottom.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in dire straits / to hit rock bottom
entries.example_es: Desde que perdí el trabajo, estoy en la olla.
entries.example_en: Since I lost my job, I've been in dire straits.

entries.literal_translation: To be without a single peso
entries.meaning_intent: To be completely broke, with no money at all.
entries.english_equivalent: To be flat broke
entries.example_es: No puedo salir hoy, estoy sin un peso hasta el próximo pago.
entries.example_en: I can't go out today, I'm flat broke until next payday.

entries.meaning_intent: To be very well off financially, loaded with money.
entries.english_equivalent: To be loaded / rolling in money
entries.example_es: Desde que le fue bien con el negocio, ese manito está forrado.
entries.example_en: Ever since the business took off, that guy is loaded.

entries.meaning_intent: To be extremely stingy or cheap with money.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a tightwad / cheapskate
entries.example_es: Nunca invita a nadie, es una mano de puerco.
entries.example_en: He never treats anyone — total cheapskate.

entries.meaning_intent: To reluctantly spend money, especially more than one wanted to.
entries.english_equivalent: To dig into your pocket / to fork over money
entries.example_es: Tocó rascarse el bolsillo para arreglar el carro.
entries.example_en: We had to dig deep into our pockets to fix the car.

entries.meaning_intent: To be financially ruined or completely out of money.
entries.english_equivalent: To be broke / bankrupt
entries.example_es: Después de esa inversión mala quedó quebrado.
entries.example_en: After that bad investment he ended up broke.

entries.meaning_intent: To work in order to support oneself or one's family; earning a living, often emphasizing honest effort.
entries.english_equivalent: To earn your bread and butter
entries.example_es: Todos los días madruga a ganarse el pan.
entries.example_en: Every day he gets up early to earn his bread and butter.

entries.meaning_intent: To ignore someone completely, to pay no attention to what they say.
entries.english_equivalent: To pay someone no mind / to blow someone off
entries.example_es: Le avisé del riesgo pero no me paró bolas.
entries.example_en: I warned him about the risk but he didn't pay me any mind.

entries.meaning_intent: To reluctantly hand over money, especially after resisting or hesitating.
entries.english_equivalent: To cough up the cash
entries.example_es: Al final tocó aflojar la plata para el arreglo.
entries.example_en: In the end we had to cough up the cash for the repair.

entries.meaning_intent: To take a bribe or profit from corruption; implies dirtying oneself with illicit money.
entries.english_equivalent: To take a bribe / to have dirty hands
entries.example_es: Dicen que el funcionario se untó las manos con ese contrato.
entries.example_en: They say the official took a bribe on that contract.

entries.meaning_intent: To run an errand or handle a pending task, often bureaucratic or logistical.
entries.english_equivalent: To run an errand
entries.example_es: Ya vengo, tengo que hacer una vuelta en el banco.
entries.example_en: Be right back, I have to run an errand at the bank.

entries.meaning_intent: To be so infatuated with someone that you humble yourself excessively to win their attention.
entries.english_equivalent: To be head over heels / to simp
entries.example_es: Ese man anda de arrastrado detrás de ella, le hace de todo.
entries.example_en: That guy is head over heels for her, he'll do anything for her.

entries.meaning_intent: To be daydreaming or so infatuated/distracted that you're not paying attention to reality.
entries.english_equivalent: To have your head in the clouds
entries.example_es: Desde que empezó a salir con ella anda en las nubes.
entries.example_en: Ever since he started dating her, he's had his head in the clouds.

entries.idiom: Meter los perros / Tirar los perros
entries.meaning_intent: To flirt persistently with someone, actively pursuing their romantic interest.
entries.english_equivalent: To hit on someone / to put the moves on someone
entries.example_es: En la fiesta le tiró los perros toda la noche.
entries.example_en: At the party he was hitting on her all night.

entries.literal_translation: To be left dressed up and all worked up
entries.meaning_intent: To be stood up after having gotten ready and excited for a date or event that falls through.
entries.english_equivalent: To be left high and dry / stood up
entries.example_es: Se arregló toda la tarde y quedó vestida y alborotada porque él nunca llegó.
entries.example_en: She spent all afternoon getting ready and got stood up because he never showed.

entries.meaning_intent: To cheat on a romantic partner.
entries.english_equivalent: To cheat on someone / to two-time someone
entries.example_es: Se enteró de que le estaba poniendo los cachos con su mejor amiga.
entries.example_en: She found out he was cheating on her with her best friend.

entries.literal_translation: To go around in the same [things]
entries.meaning_intent: To remain stuck in the same on-and-off, unresolved relationship dynamic.
entries.english_equivalent: To be back to the same old thing / on-again-off-again
entries.example_es: Esos dos siguen andando en las mismas, no terminan de aclarar nada.
entries.example_en: Those two are still on-again-off-again, they never sort anything out.

entries.meaning_intent: To end up looking bad or embarrassed after a situation, often socially or romantically.
entries.english_equivalent: To end up with egg on your face
entries.example_es: Quedó mal parado después de que ella contó lo que pasó.
entries.example_en: He ended up with egg on his face after she told everyone what happened.

entries.meaning_intent: To be an opportunistic flirt who cozies up to people for personal or material gain.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a gold-digger / a user
entries.example_es: Cuidado con esa, es una lagarta, solo anda detrás de la plata.
entries.example_en: Watch out for her, she's a gold-digger, only after the money.

entries.idiom: Comerse a alguien con los ojos
entries.literal_translation: To eat someone with your eyes
entries.meaning_intent: To stare at someone with intense desire or admiration.
entries.english_equivalent: To eye someone up / to undress someone with your eyes
entries.example_es: Se lo estaba comiendo con los ojos desde que entró.
entries.example_en: She was eyeing him up from the moment he walked in.

entries.meaning_intent: To party or go out dancing and drinking.
entries.english_equivalent: To party / to go out on the town
entries.example_es: Este sábado vamos a rumbear hasta tarde.
entries.example_en: This Saturday we're going out partying till late.

entries.meaning_intent: To currently be out partying.
entries.english_equivalent: To be out partying
entries.example_es: No contesta el celular, debe estar de rumba.
entries.example_en: He's not answering his phone, he must be out partying.

entries.meaning_intent: To get a party or gathering going, to liven things up.
entries.english_equivalent: To get the party started
entries.example_es: Llegó la música y prendió el parche.
entries.example_en: The music arrived and got the party started.

entries.idiom: Estar hasta las chanclas / hasta las manitas
entries.literal_translation: To be up to one's sandals / little hands
entries.meaning_intent: To be extremely drunk or intoxicated.
entries.english_equivalent: To be plastered / wasted
entries.example_es: Terminó hasta las chanclas después de la fiesta.
entries.example_en: He ended up completely plastered after the party.

entries.meaning_intent: To catch on to a joke, an insinuation, or the point of what's being said.
entries.english_equivalent: To catch the drift / to get it
entries.example_es: Le hice la broma y por fin cogió la caña.
entries.example_en: I made the joke and he finally caught the drift.

entries.meaning_intent: To hang out casually with a group of friends, without a specific plan.
entries.english_equivalent: To hang out / to chill with friends
entries.example_es: ¿Parchamos donde David esta noche?
entries.example_en: Want to hang out at David's place tonight?

entries.meaning_intent: A good hangout, gathering, or group of friends to spend time with.
entries.english_equivalent: A cool crew / a fun hangout
entries.example_es: Ese grupo del gimnasio es un parche bacano.
entries.example_en: That gym group is a really cool crew.

entries.meaning_intent: To be drunk, high, or full of energy and excitement, depending on context.
entries.english_equivalent: To be lit / buzzed
entries.example_es: A la medianoche ya estaba bien prendido.
entries.example_en: By midnight he was already good and lit.

entries.meaning_intent: To stay out partying all night until sunrise.
entries.english_equivalent: To party till dawn / to pull an all-nighter partying
entries.example_es: Amanecimos bailando el sábado pasado.
entries.example_en: We partied straight through till dawn last Saturday.

entries.idiom: Rumbear hasta que el cuerpo aguante
entries.literal_translation: To party until the body can take it
entries.meaning_intent: To party for as long as physically possible, without holding back.
entries.english_equivalent: To party till you drop
entries.example_es: Hoy es fiesta, vamos a rumbear hasta que el cuerpo aguante.
entries.example_en: Today's a celebration, we're partying till we drop.

entries.meaning_intent: To eat a huge amount, feasting without restraint.
entries.english_equivalent: To pig out / to feast
entries.example_es: En la fiesta de fin de año me puse las botas con la comida.
entries.example_en: At the year-end party I really pigged out on the food.

entries.literal_translation: To be worth licking your fingers over
entries.meaning_intent: Said of food that is extremely delicious.
entries.english_equivalent: To be finger-licking good
entries.example_es: Esa bandeja paisa estaba para chuparse los dedos.
entries.example_en: That bandeja paisa was finger-licking good.

entries.meaning_intent: To overeat to the point of feeling stuffed and bloated.
entries.english_equivalent: To stuff yourself silly
entries.example_es: En el almuerzo familiar me puse como una foca.
entries.example_en: At the family lunch I stuffed myself silly.

entries.meaning_intent: To believe something naively without question, falling for a lie or manipulation completely.
entries.english_equivalent: To swallow it whole / to fall for it hook, line, and sinker
entries.example_es: Le contó cualquier mentira y ella se la tragó entera.
entries.example_en: He told her some made-up story and she swallowed it whole.

entries.literal_translation: To fall like a ring on a finger
entries.meaning_intent: To arrive or fit at exactly the right moment or in exactly the right way.
entries.english_equivalent: To fit like a glove / to be just what the doctor ordered
entries.example_es: Esa plata me cayó como anillo al dedo para pagar el arriendo.
entries.example_en: That money came just when I needed it to pay rent.

entries.idiom: Írsele la mano en la sal
entries.literal_translation: For the hand to slip with the salt
entries.meaning_intent: To overdo the seasoning of a dish, or by extension, to overdo any action.
entries.english_equivalent: To overdo it / to go heavy-handed
entries.example_es: Se le fue la mano en la sal con la sopa.
entries.example_en: He went a little heavy-handed with the salt in the soup.

entries.meaning_intent: To mind your own business and not comment on or interfere in others' matters.
entries.english_equivalent: To keep your nose out of it / to eat quietly and say nothing
entries.example_es: Yo en esa discusión como callado, no es mi problema.
entries.example_en: In that argument I just keep my mouth shut, it's not my problem.

entries.meaning_intent: It rained very heavily, a sudden downpour.
entries.english_equivalent: It poured / it came down in buckets
entries.example_es: Cayó un palo de agua justo cuando salíamos de la casa.
entries.example_en: It poured down in buckets right when we were leaving the house.

entries.meaning_intent: To be a snitch or tattletale, someone who reports on others' business.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a snitch / a rat
entries.example_es: No le cuentes nada, ese man es un sapo.
entries.example_en: Don't tell him anything, that guy is a total snitch.

entries.meaning_intent: To snitch on someone, to report or tell on them.
entries.english_equivalent: To rat someone out
entries.example_es: Alguien sapeó y ahora todos saben lo que pasó.
entries.example_en: Someone ratted us out and now everyone knows what happened.

entries.literal_translation: To be a case of gonorrhea
entries.meaning_intent: A very strong, vulgar insult for a despicable or awful person — though among close friends, especially in Medellín slang, it can be used ironically/affectionately as an intensifier.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a scumbag / (affectionately, among friends) a rascal
entries.example_es: Ese manito es un gonorrea, le hizo trampa a todos.
entries.example_en: That guy is a total scumbag, he cheated everyone.

entries.meaning_intent: Vulgar but extremely common word meaning fool or idiot as an insult — yet just as often used affectionately or as a casual filler term of address among close friends ('parce', 'güevón', similar function).
entries.english_equivalent: To be an idiot / (casually, among friends) 'dude'
entries.example_es: No sea güevón, revise bien antes de firmar.
entries.example_en: Don't be an idiot, check it carefully before signing.

entries.meaning_intent: A mild way of calling someone silly or foolish, without real malice.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a silly goose
entries.example_es: No sea bobo, eso no va ahí.
entries.example_en: Don't be silly, that doesn't go there.

entries.meaning_intent: To behave with brazen disregard for propriety or others' feelings — someone who acts badly without remorse.
entries.english_equivalent: To have some nerve / to be shameless
entries.example_es: ¡Qué sinvergüenza, se comió todo y ni las gracias dio!
entries.example_en: What nerve — he ate everything and didn't even say thanks!

entries.meaning_intent: To have tacky, low-quality taste — in clothing, style, or behavior.
entries.english_equivalent: To be tacky / trashy in style
entries.example_es: Ese carro con tantas luces se ve muy mañé.
entries.example_en: That car with all those lights looks really tacky.

entries.meaning_intent: To be unrefined, coarse, or lacking in manners/style; can be an insult about class or taste.
entries.english_equivalent: To be uncouth / low-class
entries.example_es: Se comportó muy corroncho en la reunión.
entries.example_en: He acted really uncouth at the meeting.

entries.meaning_intent: To be a suck-up or flatterer who curries favor with people in power.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a brown-noser / a suck-up
entries.example_es: Siempre le hace la barra al jefe, es un lambón.
entries.example_en: He always kisses up to the boss, total suck-up.

entries.meaning_intent: To feign innocence or shyness while secretly being sly, manipulative, or up to something.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a sly one hiding behind an innocent act
entries.example_es: Parece inocente pero es una mosca muerta.
entries.example_en: She seems innocent but she's a sly one underneath.

entries.literal_translation: To play the fool / the crazy one
entries.meaning_intent: To pretend not to notice or understand something in order to avoid responsibility.
entries.english_equivalent: To play dumb
entries.example_es: Sabía del problema pero se hizo el bobo.
entries.example_en: He knew about the problem but played dumb.

entries.meaning_intent: To stir up trouble or conflict between people, often through gossip.
entries.english_equivalent: To stir the pot / to sow discord
entries.example_es: Deja de meter cizaña entre esos dos amigos.
entries.example_en: Stop stirring the pot between those two friends.

entries.meaning_intent: Cool, great, or likeable — describes people, plans, or things positively.
entries.english_equivalent: Cool / awesome
entries.example_es: Ese plan de ir a la finca está muy bacano.
entries.example_en: That plan to go to the farmhouse sounds really cool.

entries.meaning_intent: Cool, nice, or pleasant — one of the most iconic Colombian/Venezuelan approval words.
entries.english_equivalent: Cool / nice
entries.example_es: Qué chévere que por fin nos vimos.
entries.example_en: It's so nice that we finally got to see each other.

entries.meaning_intent: Extremely common, mildly vulgar exclamation meaning something is awesome or excellent.
entries.english_equivalent: How awesome! / Hell yeah!
entries.example_es: ¡Qué chimba de partido nos vimos anoche!
entries.example_en: What an awesome game we watched last night!

entries.meaning_intent: By sheer luck or accident; something that happened by pure fluke.
entries.english_equivalent: By a fluke / by pure luck
entries.example_es: Gané la rifa de chimba, ni sabía que había comprado boleta.
entries.example_en: I won the raffle by a total fluke, I didn't even know I had a ticket.

entries.meaning_intent: How great, how cool — expressing admiration or approval for something impressive.
entries.english_equivalent: How cool is that!
entries.example_es: Qué nota el concierto, quedé impresionado.
entries.example_en: That concert was so cool, I was blown away.

entries.meaning_intent: Right away, immediately, or absolutely yes — expresses enthusiastic, instant agreement or action.
entries.english_equivalent: Right away / for sure, absolutely
entries.example_es: ¿Vamos a comer? — ¡De una!
entries.example_en: Want to go eat? — Absolutely, right now!

entries.meaning_intent: Go for it, sure, let's do it — an encouraging, casual affirmation to proceed with a plan.
entries.english_equivalent: Go for it / sure, let's do it
entries.example_es: ¿Nos vamos ya? — Hágale pues.
entries.example_en: Should we head out now? — Sure, let's do it.

entries.meaning_intent: Absolutely not, no way — a firm, colorful refusal.
entries.english_equivalent: No way in hell / not a chance
entries.example_es: ¿Que le preste plata otra vez? Ni de fundas.
entries.example_en: Lend him money again? No way in hell.

entries.meaning_intent: Totally, for real, absolutely — a modern affirmation used to strongly agree with something.
entries.english_equivalent: Totally / for real
entries.example_es: ¿Esa fiesta estuvo increíble? — Sí fue.
entries.example_en: Was that party amazing? — Totally was.

entries.meaning_intent: Something going perfectly, exactly as needed or hoped.
entries.english_equivalent: Right on the money / perfect
entries.example_es: Ese horario me queda al pelo para llegar a tiempo.
entries.example_en: That schedule works perfectly for me to get there on time.

entries.meaning_intent: Something is amazing, incredible, over-the-top good.
entries.english_equivalent: To be insane (in a good way) / incredible
entries.example_es: El concierto estuvo brutal, no lo esperaba tan bueno.
entries.example_en: The concert was insane, I didn't expect it to be that good.

entries.meaning_intent: Used before a noun to mean an excellent example of that thing.
entries.english_equivalent: A killer [thing] / a badass [thing]
entries.example_es: Se compró una chimba de moto.
entries.example_en: He bought himself a killer motorcycle.

entries.meaning_intent: To be extremely angry, worked up to the point of losing composure.
entries.english_equivalent: To be fuming / seeing red
entries.example_es: Cuando se enteró de la traición quedó embalado.
entries.example_en: When he found out about the betrayal, he was fuming.

entries.literal_translation: To be made into a wild beast
entries.meaning_intent: To be furious, in a rage.
entries.english_equivalent: To be like a wild animal / furious
entries.example_es: Llegó hecho una fiera después de la reunión.
entries.example_en: He came back absolutely furious after the meeting.

entries.meaning_intent: To have a short temper, being quick to anger as a personality trait.
entries.english_equivalent: To have a short fuse
entries.example_es: No le digas nada ahorita, tiene muy mal genio.
entries.example_en: Don't say anything to him right now, he has a real short fuse.

entries.meaning_intent: To be feeling down, low energy or sad, going through an emotional low.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in a slump / feeling low
entries.example_es: Ando de bajón esta semana, no sé ni por qué.
entries.example_en: I've been in a slump this week, not even sure why.

entries.meaning_intent: To be distracted or absent-minded, not paying attention to what's happening.
entries.english_equivalent: To have your head in the clouds / to space out
entries.example_es: Perdón, estaba en la luna, ¿qué dijiste?
entries.example_en: Sorry, I was spacing out, what did you say?

entries.idiom: Írsele el alma a los pies
entries.literal_translation: For one's soul to go down to their feet
entries.meaning_intent: To feel a sudden, deep shock or devastation upon hearing bad news.
entries.english_equivalent: Your heart sinks / your stomach drops
entries.example_es: Se le fue el alma a los pies cuando le dieron la noticia.
entries.example_en: His heart sank the moment they gave him the news.

entries.literal_translation: To pull out the rock / to give rock
entries.meaning_intent: To deeply annoy or irritate someone, or to be irritated oneself ('me da piedra').
entries.english_equivalent: To get on someone's nerves / to grate on you
entries.example_es: Me saca la piedra que llegue tarde siempre.
entries.example_en: It really gets on my nerves that he's always late.

entries.meaning_intent: How tedious, annoying, or exhausting — used far beyond literal laziness, for anything that feels like a hassle or drains your energy.
entries.english_equivalent: What a drag / ugh, so annoying
entries.example_es: Qué pereza tener que madrugar mañana.
entries.example_en: What a drag having to get up early tomorrow.

entries.literal_translation: To be like water for chocolate
entries.meaning_intent: To be at the boiling point of anger, about to explode.
entries.english_equivalent: To be at a boiling point / ready to blow
entries.example_es: Con tanta demora en el trámite quedé como agua para chocolate.
entries.example_en: With all the delays in the paperwork I was at a total boiling point.

entries.literal_translation: To turn as red as a tomato
entries.meaning_intent: To blush deeply from embarrassment.
entries.english_equivalent: To turn beet red / to blush like crazy
entries.example_es: Se puso rojo como un tomate cuando lo felicitaron en público.
entries.example_en: He turned beet red when they praised him in front of everyone.

entries.literal_translation: To make the bear / what a bear
entries.meaning_intent: To embarrass yourself publicly, or to describe an embarrassing situation.
entries.english_equivalent: To make a fool of yourself / how embarrassing
entries.example_es: Hice el oso resbalando delante de todos.
entries.example_en: I made a total fool of myself slipping in front of everyone.

entries.meaning_intent: Used far beyond its literal sense as a polite, almost reflexive apology intensifier — 'sorry to bother you' or 'I'm so embarrassed', a hallmark of Colombian courtesy.
entries.english_equivalent: So sorry / I feel so bad
entries.example_es: Qué pena molestarlo, ¿me regala un minuto?
entries.example_en: So sorry to bother you, could I have a minute?

entries.idiom: Estar más perdido/a que el hijo de Lindbergh
entries.literal_translation: To be more lost than Lindbergh's son
entries.meaning_intent: To be utterly confused or lost, both literally (directions) and figuratively (not understanding a topic) — refers to the famously unsolved 1932 Lindbergh kidnapping.
entries.english_equivalent: To be totally lost / clueless
entries.example_es: En esa clase de física quedé más perdido que el hijo de Lindbergh.
entries.example_en: In that physics class I was completely and utterly lost.

entries.literal_translation: For the plane to leave on someone
entries.meaning_intent: To completely space out, lose your train of thought, or miss the point of a conversation.
entries.english_equivalent: To zone out / to totally miss it
entries.example_es: Perdón, se me fue el avión, ¿de qué estábamos hablando?
entries.example_en: Sorry, I totally zoned out, what were we talking about?

entries.idiom: Estar entre azul y buenas noches
entries.literal_translation: To be between blue and good night
entries.meaning_intent: To be undecided or confused, caught in limbo between two options.
entries.english_equivalent: To be up in the air / torn between two things
entries.example_es: Estoy entre azul y buenas noches con esas dos ofertas de trabajo.
entries.example_en: I'm torn between those two job offers.

entries.literal_translation: For the rock to fly off/away
entries.meaning_intent: To suddenly and sharply lose one's temper.
entries.english_equivalent: To fly off the handle / to lose it
entries.example_es: Se le voló la piedra y le gritó a todo el mundo.
entries.example_en: He flew off the handle and yelled at everyone.

entries.meaning_intent: To be extremely scared, frightened stiff.
entries.english_equivalent: To be scared shitless
entries.example_es: Con el temblor quedé cagado del susto.
entries.example_en: With that earthquake I was scared shitless.

entries.meaning_intent: To be so scared or moved that your hair stands on end.
entries.english_equivalent: To make your hair stand on end
entries.example_es: Con esa historia de terror se me pararon los pelos.
entries.example_en: That horror story made my hair stand on end.

entries.meaning_intent: To tremble visibly from fear or nervousness.
entries.english_equivalent: To shake like a leaf
entries.example_es: Antes de la entrevista temblaba como una hoja.
entries.example_en: Before the interview I was shaking like a leaf.

entries.literal_translation: To be lit up with rage
entries.meaning_intent: To be visibly furious, burning with anger.
entries.english_equivalent: To be burning mad
entries.example_es: Estaba prendido de ira por la injusticia del arbitraje.
entries.example_en: He was burning mad over the unfair refereeing.

entries.meaning_intent: To talk a lot of persuasive nonsense, sweet-talk, or flattery to get something from someone.
entries.english_equivalent: To sweet-talk / to feed someone a line
entries.example_es: No le eches carreta, dime la verdad de una vez.
entries.example_en: Don't sweet-talk me, just tell me the truth already.

entries.meaning_intent: To nag repeatedly about the same issue.
entries.english_equivalent: To nag / to go on and on about something
entries.example_es: Mi mamá me dio cantaleta toda la semana por el desorden.
entries.example_en: My mom nagged me all week about the mess.

entries.idiom: Meterle los dedos a la boca a alguien
entries.literal_translation: To put your fingers in someone's mouth
entries.meaning_intent: To deceive or fool someone into believing something false.
entries.english_equivalent: To pull the wool over someone's eyes
entries.example_es: Le metió los dedos a la boca y le vendió el carro dañado como nuevo.
entries.example_en: He pulled the wool over her eyes and sold her the broken car as new.

entries.meaning_intent: To soften or sugarcoat bad news before delivering it.
entries.english_equivalent: To sugarcoat it
entries.example_es: No me dores la píldora, dime qué pasó de verdad.
entries.example_en: Don't sugarcoat it, tell me what really happened.

entries.idiom: Sacar el cobre / Salírsele el cobre
entries.literal_translation: To pull out the copper / for the copper to show
entries.meaning_intent: To reveal one's true, less flattering nature or intentions after pretending otherwise.
entries.english_equivalent: To show your true colors
entries.example_es: Al final se le salió el cobre y mostró lo interesado que era.
entries.example_en: In the end his true colors showed and it was clear how self-interested he was.

entries.meaning_intent: To naively believe a lie, excuse, or manipulation without questioning it.
entries.english_equivalent: To fall for the story / to buy it
entries.example_es: Le dio cualquier excusa y se comió el cuento entero.
entries.example_en: He gave her some excuse and she totally bought it.

entries.literal_translation: To sell illusions / to sell smoke
entries.meaning_intent: To make false or exaggerated promises with no real substance behind them.
entries.english_equivalent: To sell smoke / to oversell empty promises
entries.example_es: Ese candidato solo vende humo, no tiene propuestas reales.
entries.example_en: That candidate is just selling smoke, no real proposals.

entries.meaning_intent: To skip out on paying a bill (dine-and-dash), or to stand someone up without warning.
entries.english_equivalent: To dine and dash / to skip out on someone
entries.example_es: Le hicieron conejo en el restaurante y se fueron sin pagar.
entries.example_en: They dined and dashed at the restaurant and left without paying.

entries.idiom: Hacerse el de la vista gorda
entries.meaning_intent: To deliberately turn a blind eye to something wrong happening.
entries.english_equivalent: To turn a blind eye
entries.example_es: El jefe se hace el de la vista gorda con esas llegadas tarde.
entries.example_en: The boss turns a blind eye to those late arrivals.

entries.meaning_intent: To be acting lazy or slacking off, avoiding effort.
entries.english_equivalent: To be lazing around
entries.example_es: No estés de guevón, ayúdeme a organizar esto.
entries.example_en: Stop lazing around, help me organize this.

entries.meaning_intent: To be idle, doing absolutely nothing productive.
entries.english_equivalent: To twiddle your thumbs / to laze around
entries.example_es: Mientras todos trabajaban, él se la pasó rascándose la barriga.
entries.example_en: While everyone else worked, he spent the whole time twiddling his thumbs.

entries.literal_translation: To be sprawled out like a little lizard
entries.meaning_intent: To be lounging around lazily, doing nothing, often on a couch or bed.
entries.english_equivalent: To be sprawled out like a couch potato
entries.example_es: Todo el domingo estuvo tirado como una lagartija viendo tele.
entries.example_en: All Sunday he was sprawled out like a couch potato watching TV.

entries.literal_translation: To lie down in the shade
entries.meaning_intent: To slack off or coast on effort, especially at work.
entries.english_equivalent: To coast / to slack off
entries.example_es: Desde que lo ascendieron se echó a la sombra.
entries.example_en: Ever since he got promoted he's been coasting.

entries.meaning_intent: To feel like something is too much of a hassle or too tedious to be bothered with.
entries.english_equivalent: To not be worth the hassle / to feel like a drag
entries.example_es: Me da mamera salir con este frío.
entries.example_en: It's such a drag to go out in this cold.

entries.meaning_intent: To be stuck, whether in traffic or metaphorically stuck in a life situation with no movement.
entries.english_equivalent: To be stuck / gridlocked
entries.example_es: Llevo media hora trancado en este taco.
entries.example_en: I've been stuck in this traffic jam for half an hour.

entries.meaning_intent: To be caught in heavy traffic.
entries.english_equivalent: To be stuck in a traffic jam
entries.example_es: Llego tarde, estoy en un taco tremendo en la autopista.
entries.example_en: I'll be late, I'm stuck in a huge traffic jam on the highway.

entries.meaning_intent: To move or act very quickly, rushing.
entries.english_equivalent: To go a mile a minute / to rush
entries.example_es: Hoy ando a mil, tengo mil vueltas por hacer.
entries.example_en: I'm going a mile a minute today, so many errands to run.

entries.meaning_intent: To take pride in and openly show off an achievement.
entries.english_equivalent: To puff out your chest / to take pride in something publicly
entries.example_es: Después de ganar el premio, sacó pecho con todos.
entries.example_en: After winning the award, he puffed out his chest to everyone.

entries.meaning_intent: Casual greeting meaning 'what's up' or 'how's it going'.
entries.english_equivalent: What's up? / What's good?
entries.example_es: ¡Quiubo parce! ¿Cómo vamos?
entries.example_en: What's up, man! How's it going?

entries.meaning_intent: Casual way of asking how someone's doing, expecting an easy affirmative.
entries.english_equivalent: You good?
entries.example_es: ¿Todo bien o qué, parcero?
entries.example_en: Everything good, or what, man?

entries.meaning_intent: A quick warning to pay attention or be careful, shortened from 'ponte las pilas'.
entries.english_equivalent: Heads up! / Watch out!
entries.example_es: Pilas con ese vendedor, siempre cobra de más.
entries.example_en: Heads up with that vendor, he always overcharges.

entries.meaning_intent: To suddenly realize or understand something you hadn't grasped before.
entries.english_equivalent: To realize / for it to click
entries.example_es: Solo hasta ahora caí en cuenta de lo que quiso decir.
entries.example_en: It only just clicked for me what he meant.

entries.meaning_intent: To be aware, informed, or in the loop about a situation.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in the loop / clued in
entries.example_es: Tranquilo, yo estoy en el cuento de lo que pasó.
entries.example_en: Relax, I'm in the loop on what happened.

entries.meaning_intent: To take charge, assert authority, or finally act with determination in a situation.
entries.english_equivalent: To man up / to take control
entries.example_es: Ya tocó ponerse los pantalones y tomar la decisión.
entries.example_en: It was time to man up and make the decision.

entries.meaning_intent: To get one's way despite obstacles or others' objections.
entries.english_equivalent: To get your way
entries.example_es: Al final siempre se sale con la suya.
entries.example_en: In the end he always gets his way.

entries.meaning_intent: Watch out, pay attention — a sharp warning to be alert.
entries.english_equivalent: Watch out! / Heads up!
entries.example_es: ¡Ojo con ese hueco en la calle!
entries.example_en: Watch out for that pothole in the street!

entries.meaning_intent: Reassuring phrase used to de-escalate tension or confirm that everything is fine.
entries.english_equivalent: It's all good / all cool
entries.example_es: Tranquilo, todo bien, todo bien, no pasó nada grave.
entries.example_en: Relax, it's all good, nothing serious happened.

entries.meaning_intent: Close friend, buddy, pal — Colombia's most iconic term of camaraderie, born in Medellín and now used nationwide.
entries.english_equivalent: Bro / buddy / dude
entries.example_es: ¿Quiubo parce, todo bien?
entries.example_en: What's up, buddy? Everything good?

entries.meaning_intent: To feel at home and comfortable somewhere, so much so that you don't want to leave.
entries.english_equivalent: To feel right at home / settled in
entries.example_es: Estoy muy amañado en esta ciudad, no me quiero ir.
entries.example_en: I feel so at home in this city, I don't want to leave.

entries.meaning_intent: To show off or draw attention to oneself, often in an exaggerated or attention-seeking way.
entries.english_equivalent: To grandstand / to make a scene to be noticed
entries.example_es: Deja de hacer visajes, nadie te está mirando.
entries.example_en: Stop trying to show off, nobody's watching you.

entries.meaning_intent: To meet up specifically to have a small black coffee and chat.
entries.english_equivalent: To grab a coffee and catch up
entries.example_es: ¿Vamos a tintiar mañana y me cuenta cómo le fue?
entries.example_en: Want to grab a coffee tomorrow and tell me how it went?

entries.meaning_intent: Depending on tone, either tacky/vulgar in style, or funny/goofy — context and delivery decide which.
entries.english_equivalent: Tacky / (or) goofy, hilarious
entries.example_es: Ese chiste estuvo bien charro, me reí un montón.
entries.example_en: That joke was hilarious, I laughed so much.

entries.idiom: A otro perro con ese hueso
entries.literal_translation: To another dog with that bone
entries.meaning_intent: Used to dismiss someone's attempt to fool or manipulate you — you're not buying it.
entries.english_equivalent: Tell it to someone else / not buying it
entries.example_es: ¿Que se te olvidó la plata? A otro perro con ese hueso.
entries.example_en: You 'forgot' the money? Tell it to someone else.

entries.meaning_intent: Advice that the best way to get over heartbreak is to move on to a new interest or distraction.
entries.english_equivalent: The best way to get over someone is to get under someone new
entries.example_es: Anímate a salir con alguien más, un clavo saca otro clavo.
entries.example_en: Go out with someone else, cheer up — a new nail drives out the old one.

entries.meaning_intent: Exclamation of surprise, frustration, or annoyance.
entries.english_equivalent: Damn! / Ugh, geez!
entries.example_es: ¡Erda! Se me quedaron las llaves adentro.
entries.example_en: Damn it! I locked my keys inside.

entries.meaning_intent: What a shame or pity — expressing sympathy for someone's misfortune.
entries.english_equivalent: What a shame / poor thing
entries.example_es: Qué pecao con esa señora, le robaron todo.
entries.example_en: What a shame for that lady, they stole everything from her.

entries.literal_translation: To be settled in with someone
entries.meaning_intent: To feel deeply comfortable and bonded with a person or group.
entries.english_equivalent: To really click with someone / to feel at home with someone
entries.example_es: Ya estoy bien amañado con ese grupo de trabajo.
entries.example_en: I really click with that work team now.

entries.meaning_intent: Depending on context: to be angry, or to describe a situation as extremely difficult; also 'ser berraco' means to be tough/impressively capable.
entries.english_equivalent: To be pissed off / (or) tough as nails / (or) really hard [situation]
entries.example_es: Ese examen estuvo bien berraco, casi nadie pasó.
entries.example_en: That exam was brutally hard, almost nobody passed.

entries.literal_translation: To be made into a ball / made into dust
entries.meaning_intent: To be utterly exhausted, physically wrecked.
entries.english_equivalent: To be beat / wiped out
entries.example_es: Después de la maratón quedé hecho pelota.
entries.example_en: After the marathon I was totally wiped out.

entries.literal_translation: To be in a bad temperament
entries.meaning_intent: To be in a bad mood, irritable, on edge.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in a foul mood
entries.example_es: No le hable ahora, está de mal genio.
entries.example_en: Don't talk to him right now, he's in a foul mood.

entries.meaning_intent: Extremely versatile Caribbean-coast filler word used to greet, agree, answer the phone, or prompt someone to continue talking.
entries.english_equivalent: Yeah? / Uh-huh / So?
entries.example_es: Ajá, ¿y entonces qué pasó?
entries.example_en: So, and then what happened?

entries.meaning_intent: Stop gossiping or stirring up chisme.
entries.english_equivalent: Stop the gossip / cut the chatter
entries.example_es: Deja el güiro y cuéntame qué pasó de verdad.
entries.example_en: Cut the gossip and tell me what really happened.

entries.meaning_intent: Playful teasing remark when someone shows up with a drastic new haircut.
entries.english_equivalent: Whoa, who did that to your hair? / Nice haircut, what happened?
entries.example_es: ¡Uy, te caíste del bus! ¿Quién te cortó el pelo así?
entries.example_en: Whoa, who did that to your hair? Who cut it like that?

entries.meaning_intent: Unrefined or tacky, originally coastal slang now used nationwide (see co058).
entries.english_equivalent: Uncouth / low-class
entries.example_es: Ese modo de hablarle a la gente es muy corroncho.
entries.example_en: That way of talking to people is really uncouth.

entries.meaning_intent: A group or gang of friends, or in some contexts a criminal gang.
entries.english_equivalent: A crew / a gang
entries.example_es: Todo el combo del barrio se fue de paseo.
entries.example_en: The whole neighborhood crew went on a trip.

entries.literal_translation: To have a tail on someone
entries.meaning_intent: To hold a grudge or resentment against someone.
entries.english_equivalent: To hold a grudge against someone
entries.example_es: Todavía le tengo cola por lo que me hizo el año pasado.
entries.example_en: I still hold a grudge against him for what he did last year.

entries.meaning_intent: Exclamation of surprise or mild disbelief.
entries.english_equivalent: Whoa! / No way!
entries.example_es: ¡Eche! No sabía que te habías graduado ya.
entries.example_en: Whoa! I didn't know you'd already graduated.

entries.meaning_intent: An extremely versatile filler noun for 'thing' or 'stuff', used for almost anything, good or bad.
entries.english_equivalent: That thing / that stuff
entries.example_es: Esa vaina que me regalaste me encantó.
entries.example_en: That thing you gave me, I loved it.

entries.meaning_intent: To be extremely hungry.
entries.english_equivalent: To be starving
entries.example_es: Tengo un filo tenaz, no he comido desde el desayuno.
entries.example_en: I'm starving, I haven't eaten since breakfast.

entries.literal_translation: To wake up with your tail up
entries.meaning_intent: To wake up in a bad, irritable mood for no clear reason.
entries.english_equivalent: To wake up on the wrong side of the bed
entries.example_es: No le hables hoy, amaneció con la cola parada.
entries.example_en: Don't talk to her today, she woke up on the wrong side of the bed.

entries.meaning_intent: A conversational filler used at the start of a sentence or to express surprise, iconic to Bogotá speech.
entries.english_equivalent: Hey! / Oh wow!
entries.example_es: ¡Ala! ¿Y usted desde cuándo por acá?
entries.example_en: Hey! Since when are you around here?

entries.literal_translation: To be at the curubito (a Bogotá hilltop landmark)
entries.meaning_intent: To be in a favorable, prominent, or advantageous position.
entries.english_equivalent: To be sitting pretty / on top of the world
entries.example_es: Desde que lo ascendieron está en el curubito.
entries.example_en: Ever since he got promoted he's been sitting pretty.

entries.meaning_intent: Said when someone exaggerated an effort or performance for show, often theatrically.
entries.english_equivalent: To go all out / to really put on a show
entries.example_es: En la presentación se dio garra bailando.
entries.example_en: In the presentation he really went all out dancing.

entries.meaning_intent: A proper, formal, well-mannered Bogotá native — can be used with admiration or as gentle teasing about being uptight/old-fashioned.
entries.english_equivalent: A proper Bogotá gent / (teasingly) stuffy
entries.example_es: Es bien cachaco, siempre con corbata hasta para ir al parque.
entries.example_en: He's so proper, always in a tie even to go to the park.

entries.meaning_intent: An old-fashioned, respectful form of 'you', typical of Bogotá/Cundiboyacá speech, now often used affectionately or humorously.
entries.english_equivalent: You (formal, old-fashioned) / 'kind sir/madam'
entries.example_es: ¿Sumercé cómo ha estado, tanto tiempo sin verlo?
entries.example_en: How have you been, sir? It's been so long.

entries.literal_translation: To go around with a peeled eye
entries.meaning_intent: To stay alert and watchful, especially of danger or opportunity.
entries.english_equivalent: To keep your eyes peeled
entries.example_es: En esa zona hay que andar con el ojo pelado.
entries.example_en: In that area you have to keep your eyes peeled.

entries.meaning_intent: To be a rowdy, loud, showy person who draws attention through boisterous behavior.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a loudmouth / a show-off
entries.example_es: Bájele al volumen, no sea tan aletoso.
entries.example_en: Turn it down, don't be such a loudmouth.

entries.meaning_intent: Exclamation of surprise, frustration, or shock.
entries.english_equivalent: Damn it! / Holy cow!
entries.example_es: ¡Juemadre! Casi me estrello con esa moto.
entries.example_en: Holy cow! I almost crashed into that motorcycle.

entries.meaning_intent: Friendly greeting using 'mono/a' as an affectionate term of address for a light-haired or light-skinned person, widely used in Valle del Cauca but heard nationwide.
entries.english_equivalent: What's up, blondie?
entries.example_es: ¿Qué hubo mono, todo bien por allá?
entries.example_en: What's up, blondie, everything good over there?

entries.meaning_intent: To be very energetic, hyperactive, or wound up.
entries.english_equivalent: To be full of energy / wound up
entries.example_es: Los niños están como una moto después de tanto dulce.
entries.example_en: The kids are wound up after all that candy.

entries.meaning_intent: In Santander, primarily used to mean angry or upset; can also mean impressively tough or difficult depending on context (note: in some other Latin American countries the word carries a sexual connotation, which is not its primary Santander meaning).
entries.english_equivalent: To be pissed off / (or) tough as nails
entries.example_es: Quedó muy arrecho porque le cancelaron el vuelo.
entries.example_en: He got really pissed off because they cancelled his flight.

entries.meaning_intent: Affectionate Santander term for grandmother.
entries.english_equivalent: Grandma
entries.example_es: Vamos a visitar a la nona este fin de semana.
entries.example_en: We're going to visit grandma this weekend.

entries.meaning_intent: Casual way to get someone's attention, similar to 'hey man, listen'.
entries.english_equivalent: Hey man, listen
entries.example_es: Oiga mano, ¿me hace un favor?
entries.example_en: Hey man, can you do me a favor?

entries.meaning_intent: To be very annoyed or angry (shared usage with llanero speech).
entries.english_equivalent: To be irritated / worked up
entries.example_es: Se embejucó porque le dañaron la herramienta nueva.
entries.example_en: He got really annoyed because they broke his new tool.

entries.meaning_intent: To become annoyed, irritated, or angry.
entries.english_equivalent: To get riled up / worked up
entries.example_es: Se embejucó con el retraso del bus.
entries.example_en: He got riled up over the bus delay.

entries.literal_translation: To go around like a bolting horse
entries.meaning_intent: To act wildly or recklessly, out of control, without restraint — image drawn from an unbroken horse that has bolted.
entries.english_equivalent: To run wild / to be out of control
entries.example_es: Desde que le dieron el carro anda como caballo desbocado.
entries.example_en: Ever since they gave him the car he's been running wild.

entries.meaning_intent: To be a very thin, scrawny person or animal.
entries.english_equivalent: To be scrawny as a rail
entries.example_es: El potrico ese está bien langaruto, hay que alimentarlo mejor.
entries.example_en: That colt is scrawny as a rail, he needs better feeding.

entries.meaning_intent: Llanero term for a close friend or buddy.
entries.english_equivalent: Buddy / pal
entries.example_es: Ese es mi camarita desde niños.
entries.example_en: That's my buddy since we were kids.

entries.idiom: El pueblo lejos y los caballos cansados
entries.literal_translation: The town far away and the horses tired
entries.meaning_intent: Said of a complicated, wearying situation with no easy or quick way out.
entries.english_equivalent: It's a long road ahead with no shortcuts / we're not out of the woods yet
entries.example_es: Con esa deuda, el pueblo lejos y los caballos cansados.
entries.example_en: With that debt, it's a long road ahead and no shortcuts in sight.

entries.idiom: La soga revienta por lo más delgado
entries.literal_translation: The rope snaps at its thinnest point
entries.meaning_intent: Trouble or blame tends to fall hardest on the weakest or most vulnerable party, or a plan fails at its weakest link.
entries.english_equivalent: A chain is only as strong as its weakest link
entries.example_es: En esa empresa, cuando hay problemas, la soga siempre revienta por lo más delgado.
entries.example_en: At that company, when there's trouble, it always falls on the weakest link.

entries.meaning_intent: To be following or aware of an ongoing conversation, gossip, or group dynamic, often on WhatsApp/social media.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in the loop / following the group chat drama
entries.example_es: ¿Ya viste lo que pasó? Yo ya estoy en el chat.
entries.example_en: Did you see what happened? I'm already in the loop.

entries.meaning_intent: To be left on read — someone saw your message but didn't reply.
entries.english_equivalent: To be left on read
entries.example_es: Le escribí hace dos días y me dejó en visto.
entries.example_en: I texted him two days ago and he left me on read.

entries.meaning_intent: To suddenly cut off all contact with someone, especially a romantic interest, without explanation.
entries.english_equivalent: To ghost someone
entries.example_es: Estábamos hablando bien y de la nada me ghosteó.
entries.example_en: We were talking fine and out of nowhere he ghosted me.

entries.meaning_intent: To make a veiled comment or post aimed at someone specific without naming them, often on social media.
entries.english_equivalent: To subtweet / to drop a not-so-subtle hint
entries.example_es: Sube puras indirectas en el estado, todos sabemos que es por ella.
entries.example_en: She keeps subtweeting on her status, we all know it's about her.

entries.meaning_intent: Younger-generation synonym for a close friend, similar to 'parcero'.
entries.english_equivalent: My guy / my ride-or-die
entries.example_es: Ese manito es mi llave desde el colegio.
entries.example_en: That guy has been my ride-or-die since school.

entries.meaning_intent: Youth-slang intensifier meaning 'very', placed before an adjective.
entries.english_equivalent: To be super / really [adjective]
entries.example_es: Esa película estuvo buti buena.
entries.example_en: That movie was really, really good.

entries.meaning_intent: To go unresponsive and ignore everyone, as if you'd switched your phone to airplane mode.
entries.english_equivalent: To go dark / to be unreachable on purpose
entries.example_es: Después del examen me puse en modo avión todo el fin de semana.
entries.example_en: After the exam I went dark all weekend.

entries.literal_translation: To put zero balls on it
entries.meaning_intent: To completely ignore something or pay it zero attention, often deliberately.
entries.english_equivalent: To pay zero mind to it / to not care at all
entries.example_es: Le puse cero bolas al comentario, no vale la pena pelear por eso.
entries.example_en: I paid zero mind to the comment, not worth fighting over.

entries.meaning_intent: No problem, no drama — everything is fine and relaxed.
entries.english_equivalent: No worries / no drama
entries.example_es: Tranquilo, cero rollo, lo resolvemos después.
entries.example_en: Relax, no worries, we'll sort it out later.

entries.meaning_intent: To show your true character or determination when it truly matters, especially under pressure.
entries.english_equivalent: To show what you're made of
entries.example_es: En el partido final el equipo sacó la casta y ganó.
entries.example_en: In the final match the team showed what they were made of and won.

entries.meaning_intent: To root for two people to become a romantic couple, especially used online about celebrities, characters, or friends.
entries.english_equivalent: To ship a couple
entries.example_es: Todo el internet está shippeando a esos dos actores.
entries.example_en: The whole internet is shipping those two actors.

entries.meaning_intent: Used as an intensifier meaning something is amazing, wild, or over the top — not literal insanity.
entries.english_equivalent: Insane (in a good way) / wild
entries.example_es: El concierto fue una locura, la gente enloqueció.
entries.example_en: The concert was insane, people went wild.

entries.meaning_intent: To be completely full of something — busy, tired, or filled up on food, used as a versatile modern intensifier.
entries.english_equivalent: To be totally packed / swamped
entries.example_es: Esta semana estoy full de trabajo, no tengo tiempo para nada.
entries.example_en: This week I'm totally swamped with work, no time for anything.

entries.meaning_intent: To be aware of and involved in what's currently happening or being planned.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in on it / to be plugged in
entries.example_es: No se preocupe que yo ya estoy en la jugada con ese proyecto.
entries.example_en: Don't worry, I'm already in on that project.

entries.meaning_intent: To rub someone the wrong way, to be disliked by someone despite not doing anything overtly wrong.
entries.english_equivalent: To rub someone the wrong way
entries.example_es: No sé por qué, pero ese man me cae gordo.
entries.example_en: I don't know why, but that guy just rubs me the wrong way.

entries.idiom: Camarón que se duerme, se lo lleva la corriente
entries.literal_translation: The shrimp that falls asleep gets carried off by the current
entries.meaning_intent: Widely used across the Spanish-speaking world but a daily-life staple in Colombia: if you're not alert and quick to act, you'll miss your chance or get taken advantage of.
entries.english_equivalent: You snooze, you lose
entries.example_es: Ya se acabaron las entradas, camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente.
entries.example_en: The tickets are already gone — you snooze, you lose.

entries.idiom: El que no llora no mama
entries.literal_translation: He who doesn't cry doesn't nurse
entries.meaning_intent: Pan-Hispanic saying, constantly used in Colombia: if you don't speak up and ask for what you need, you won't get it.
entries.english_equivalent: The squeaky wheel gets the grease
entries.example_es: Pida el aumento sin miedo, el que no llora no mama.
entries.example_en: Ask for the raise without fear, the squeaky wheel gets the grease.

entries.idiom: En boca cerrada no entran moscas
entries.literal_translation: Flies don't enter a closed mouth
entries.meaning_intent: Widely used proverb advising that staying quiet keeps you out of trouble.
entries.english_equivalent: Silence is golden / keep your mouth shut and stay out of trouble
entries.example_es: Mejor no opine de eso, en boca cerrada no entran moscas.
entries.example_en: Better not comment on that — silence is golden.

entries.idiom: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando
entries.literal_translation: A bird in hand is worth more than a hundred flying
entries.meaning_intent: It's better to keep a sure, smaller gain than risk it chasing a bigger, uncertain one.
entries.english_equivalent: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
entries.example_es: Acepte esa oferta segura, más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.
entries.example_en: Take that sure offer, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

entries.idiom: Al que madruga, Dios lo ayuda
entries.literal_translation: God helps the one who wakes up early
entries.meaning_intent: Being proactive and getting an early start leads to better results.
entries.english_equivalent: The early bird catches the worm
entries.example_es: Salimos desde las cinco de la mañana, al que madruga Dios lo ayuda.
entries.example_en: We left at five in the morning, the early bird catches the worm.

entries.idiom: Cría fama y échate a dormir
entries.literal_translation: Build a reputation and go lie down to sleep
entries.meaning_intent: Once you earn a certain reputation (good or bad), it will follow you regardless of what you do afterward.
entries.english_equivalent: Give a dog a bad name (and it will stick)
entries.example_es: Desde ese error nadie confía en él, cría fama y échate a dormir.
entries.example_en: Ever since that mistake nobody trusts him — once the reputation sticks, it sticks.

entries.literal_translation: To be like fallen from the sky
entries.meaning_intent: To arrive or appear at exactly the right, most needed moment.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a godsend / to show up like a blessing
entries.example_es: Esa ayuda llegó como caída del cielo.
entries.example_en: That help arrived like an absolute godsend.

entries.meaning_intent: To commit fully and show loyalty or dedication to a cause, team, or project.
entries.english_equivalent: To be all in / to give it your all
entries.example_es: Todo el equipo se puso la camiseta para sacar el proyecto adelante.
entries.example_en: The whole team was all in to get the project done.

entries.literal_translation: For the saint to slip off to heaven
entries.meaning_intent: To completely forget what you were about to say or do, mid-action.
entries.english_equivalent: To have a total memory blank / to lose your train of thought
entries.example_es: Se me fue el santo al cielo, ya no me acuerdo qué le iba a decir.
entries.example_en: I totally lost my train of thought, I don't remember what I was about to say.

entries.idiom: Estar como pez en el agua
entries.literal_translation: To be like a fish in water
entries.meaning_intent: To feel completely comfortable and confident in a particular environment or situation.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in your element
entries.example_es: En esa fiesta estaba como pez en el agua, conocía a todo el mundo.
entries.example_en: At that party he was totally in his element, he knew everyone.

entries.literal_translation: To 'coleo' someone (grab a running bull by the tail to floor it)
entries.meaning_intent: To intervene forcefully and stop someone or something in its tracks, drawn from the traditional llanero rodeo sport of coleo.
entries.english_equivalent: To cut someone off at the knees / to stop someone dead in their tracks
entries.example_es: Iba a firmar el contrato pero el abogado lo coleó a tiempo.
entries.example_en: He was about to sign the contract but the lawyer stopped him dead in his tracks just in time.

entries.idiom: Dar la mano al que llega
entries.literal_translation: To offer your hand to whoever arrives
entries.meaning_intent: A core llanero hospitality norm — to welcome and help any visitor or newcomer without hesitation.
entries.english_equivalent: To always welcome a stranger with open arms
entries.example_es: En el llano es ley dar la mano al que llega, así no lo conozcan.
entries.example_en: In the plains it's an unwritten law to welcome whoever arrives, even a total stranger.

entries.literal_translation: To go around remounted / retreated into the backcountry
entries.meaning_intent: To withdraw from social life, becoming reclusive or hard to reach, as if retreating deep into isolated terrain.
entries.english_equivalent: To go off the grid / to become a recluse
entries.example_es: Desde que renunció anda remontado, nadie sabe de él.
entries.example_en: Ever since he quit, he's gone completely off the grid, nobody's heard from him.

entries.meaning_intent: To be an unruly, undisciplined, hard-to-control person, especially a young one.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a wild colt / a real handful
entries.example_es: Ese muchacho es un potro sin domar, no hay quien lo controle.
entries.example_en: That kid is a wild colt, nobody can control him.

entries.idiom: Estirar más que cuero de barriga
entries.literal_translation: To stretch more than belly hide
entries.meaning_intent: To give or yield far more than expected — extremely generous or productive.
entries.english_equivalent: To go above and beyond / to stretch way further than expected
entries.example_es: Esa cosecha estiró más que cuero de barriga este año.
entries.example_en: That harvest went way above and beyond what we expected this year.

entries.idiom: Como avispa que el cigarrón es venenoso
entries.literal_translation: Like the wasp warns that the beetle is poisonous
entries.meaning_intent: A call to stay alert and cautious, watching closely for hidden danger.
entries.english_equivalent: Keep your guard up / stay sharp, danger can be anywhere
entries.example_es: Ojo con ese negocio, como avispa que el cigarrón es venenoso.
entries.example_en: Watch out with that deal, keep your guard up, danger can hide anywhere.

entries.meaning_intent: The situation is very difficult, complicated, or intense.
entries.english_equivalent: Things are rough / it's a tough situation
entries.example_es: Con tanto tráfico y el paro, está arrecha la joda para llegar al trabajo.
entries.example_en: With all the traffic and the strike, it's rough getting to work these days.

entries.meaning_intent: In Santander, a strongly positive term for someone tough, resourceful, and capable who doesn't give up in the face of hardship.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a tough, capable go-getter
entries.example_es: Ese man es un berraco, sacó a su familia adelante solo.
entries.example_en: That guy is a real go-getter, he raised his whole family on his own.

entries.meaning_intent: To be a fool or silly person, said with mild teasing.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a goof / a silly fool
entries.example_es: No sea toche, eso no se hace así.
entries.example_en: Don't be a goof, that's not how you do it.

entries.meaning_intent: To be mischievous or a troublemaker, usually said fondly about a playful child.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a little rascal
entries.example_es: Ese niño es un pingo, no para de hacer travesuras.
entries.example_en: That kid is a little rascal, he never stops with the mischief.

entries.meaning_intent: A blunt, somewhat rude way to tell someone to stop talking or shut up.
entries.english_equivalent: To shut your trap
entries.example_es: Le tocó cerrar la jeta cuando el jefe lo puso en su lugar.
entries.example_en: He had to shut his trap when the boss put him in his place.

entries.meaning_intent: A dismissive, contemptuous way to refer to someone, often a misbehaving child.
entries.english_equivalent: That little runt / that brat
entries.example_es: Ese petuste no deja de molestar a los demás niños.
entries.example_en: That little brat won't stop bothering the other kids.

entries.meaning_intent: An attention-getting filler particle used constantly in Cali speech, similar to 'hey' or 'listen', often tacked onto the start or end of a sentence.
entries.english_equivalent: Hey! / Look here!
entries.example_es: Ve, ¿usted ya vio lo que pasó allá afuera?
entries.example_en: Hey, did you already see what happened outside?

entries.literal_translation: To open oneself away from the hangout
entries.meaning_intent: To leave a gathering or head out, to bounce from where you are.
entries.english_equivalent: To bounce / to head out
entries.example_es: Ya me voy a abrir del parche, mañana madrugo.
entries.example_en: I'm gonna bounce now, I have to get up early tomorrow.

entries.meaning_intent: To go out cruising or wandering around with friends with no particular destination, just for the sake of it.
entries.english_equivalent: To go cruising around / joyriding with friends
entries.example_es: Vamos a dar una borondeada por el centro esta tarde.
entries.example_en: Let's go cruise around downtown this afternoon.

entries.meaning_intent: A preppy, wealthy, image-conscious young person, often used with a hint of mockery about their privileged bubble.
entries.english_equivalent: To be a preppy rich kid
entries.example_es: Ese manito es bien gomelo, todo lo que usa es de marca.
entries.example_en: That guy is such a preppy rich kid, everything he wears is designer.

entries.meaning_intent: A term for a rough, streetwise, lower-class person; can be descriptive but is often pejorative and classist, so context and tone matter a lot.
entries.english_equivalent: To be rough around the edges / (used pejoratively) a hoodlum
entries.example_es: Ojo con esa zona de noche, es bien ñera.
entries.example_en: Watch out with that area at night, it's pretty rough.

entries.meaning_intent: A common Bogotá / central-Colombia word for a child or kid, unrelated to nationality.
entries.english_equivalent: A kid
entries.example_es: Ese chino no para de correr por toda la casa.
entries.example_en: That kid won't stop running all over the house.

entries.meaning_intent: Extremely common way to refer to 'that guy' or 'that girl', especially among Bogotá youth, now heard nationwide.
entries.english_equivalent: That guy / that girl
entries.example_es: Ese man no ha llegado todavía.
entries.example_en: That guy still hasn't shown up.

entries.literal_translation: To be in a bad coffee
entries.meaning_intent: To be in a bad, irritable mood.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in a foul mood
entries.example_es: No le hable ahorita, está de mal café.
entries.example_en: Don't talk to him right now, he's in a foul mood.

entries.meaning_intent: To be smart, sharp, and quick to catch on — a term so iconic it named Colombia's national merit scholarship program 'Ser Pilo Paga'.
entries.english_equivalent: To be sharp / a quick study
entries.example_es: Esa niña es bien pila, aprende todo rapidísimo.
entries.example_en: That girl is really sharp, she picks everything up so fast.

entries.meaning_intent: To have style, swagger, or a distinctive way of carrying yourself, especially tied to music/fashion culture.
entries.english_equivalent: To have swagger
entries.example_es: Ese manito baila con mucho flow.
entries.example_en: That guy dances with a lot of swagger.

entries.meaning_intent: To be aware of or caught up in what's currently trending or being discussed on social media.
entries.english_equivalent: To be plugged into what's trending online
entries.example_es: No sabía nada de eso, no ando en el timeline últimamente.
entries.example_en: I had no idea about that, I haven't been keeping up online lately.

entries.meaning_intent: To be sore, irritated, or bothered about losing or being outdone at something, especially competitively.
entries.english_equivalent: To be salty about losing
entries.example_es: Quedó picado porque le ganamos el partido.
entries.example_en: He's salty because we beat him at the game.

entries.literal_translation: Adapted from English 'cringe', built into a Colombian Spanish grammatical frame with 'dar'
entries.meaning_intent: To feel secondhand embarrassment watching or hearing something awkward.
entries.english_equivalent: It makes me cringe
entries.example_es: Me da cringe ver esos videos tan forzados.
entries.example_en: Those forced videos make me cringe so hard.

entries.literal_translation: To throw / throw yourself a ticket
entries.meaning_intent: To accidentally reveal something you were trying to hide, giving yourself away.
entries.english_equivalent: To blow your own cover / to give yourself away
entries.example_es: Se tiró la boleta al mencionar el regalo antes de tiempo.
entries.example_en: He gave himself away by mentioning the gift too early.

entries.meaning_intent: To be caught up in gossip or drama, or the gossip/drama itself.
entries.english_equivalent: To be in on the drama / the tea
entries.example_es: Cuénteme el salseo completo, no me deje con las ganas.
entries.example_en: Tell me all the drama, don't leave me hanging.

entries.meaning_intent: For a post, video, or moment to spread rapidly and widely on social media.
entries.english_equivalent: To go viral
entries.example_es: Ese video quedó viral en cuestión de horas.
entries.example_en: That video went viral within hours.

entries.meaning_intent: To be in tune with what's currently happening or expected, on the same wavelength as everyone else.
entries.english_equivalent: To be on the same page / in tune with what's going on
entries.example_es: Tranquilo que yo ya estoy en la nota de lo que se viene.
entries.example_en: Relax, I'm already on the same page about what's coming.

entries.meaning_intent: To be the person someone has a romantic crush on.
entries.english_equivalent: To be someone's crush
entries.example_es: Ella es el crush de medio salón.
entries.example_en: She's the crush of half the classroom.
